newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March real earnings rose 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March real earnings rose 0.1 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 0.1 percent in March, the Labor Department said Tuesday.
The March increase followed a revised 2.3 percent jump in February real average weekly earnings. Previously, the department reported that February real earnings rose 2.4 percent.

The March rise stems from a 0.4 percent increase in average hourly earnings, which was offset by a 0.3 percent decrease in average weekly hours, the Labor Department said. The 0.1 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers also contributed to the modest increase.
Real average weekly earnings in March were 2.6 percent above the March 1996 level, Labor reported.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $261.00 in March, versus a revised $260.83 in February and $255.36 in March 1996.
The department had previously reported February weekly earnings at $261.37.

In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $422.82 in March, compared with a revised $422.29 in February and $402.96 in March last year. The deparment had previously reported February current dollar earnings at $423.15.
